Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-3-prompt-long-0100", "row_sha256": "0d891db083b608c449b3c5b3a0d312c20e69703c800d1e36dda674d105aefed8", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
can you turn this into a clear prompt for an internal product update, not write the update itself. it’s about the restore preference in Finch Tabs, our fictional browser extension, and should read like a straightforward update for the product, support, and documentation teams. keep it self-contained and use the facts here, including the limitations and the last assessment. i have notes from a few places so they’re a bit jumbled.

The preference is called “Restore the last tab group when the browser starts.” It’s in Settings > Startup in Finch Tabs version 2.8.1. It is off by default, and a person has to turn it on and save the setting; nothing changes for existing users just because they install 2.8.1. The checkbox itself can be changed without restarting the browser, but its effect is only seen at the next full browser launch. That distinction matters, since a few support messages described the setting as taking effect immediately. Don’t say that it restores every window or every kind of session. The behavior is limited to the last non-private tab group in the same browser profile. It doesn’t bring back private windows, and it doesn’t merge tab groups from two profiles.

There’s also a condition about startup behavior that needs to be in the update, not buried or silently dropped. The preference is available when the user’s Startup choice is “New tab”; when a different startup choice is selected, the checkbox is unavailable. If someone enables the preference and later changes the startup choice, the saved preference remains on, but the restore behavior is not used while that other choice is active. If they select “New tab” again, the saved preference applies at the next full launch. The setting is local to each browser profile. Finch Tabs sync does not copy it between profiles or devices. Mention that plainly, but don’t imply the setting is broken when a second device has a different value.

The 2.8.1 desktop beta is currently available to 15 percent of eligible profiles, with the staged rollout beginning on May 6. The beta is limited to desktop installations that are not managed by an organization. The mobile companion does not have this preference. Do not describe this as a release to everyone or imply that the mobile app is scheduled to get it. There isn’t a confirmed expansion date in the notes. Product has asked for an update on what the preference does and what the first feedback says; they have not asked us to announce a rollout decision.

The early assessment covers the first 12 days after the beta began, through May 18, and includes 214 opted-in desktop profiles. Support logged 17 messages that mentioned the preference during that period. Of those, 9 asked where to find the checkbox, 5 described expecting restoration before the next full launch, and 3 asked why the preference wasn’t available on a managed installation. Keep these as counts of messages, not people or confirmed defects. They don’t establish how common the same expectations are among all Finch Tabs users. One support note said, “I want my work tabs back, but not the window I closed on purpose.” It was a comment about the preference’s intended scope, not a report that private windows had actually been restored. Keep the quote in ordinary reported context and don’t turn it into a general customer conclusion.

For the update, explain the setting in plain language before describing the feedback. It may help to distinguish saving the checkbox from when the browser uses the saved choice. Include the rollout status and the feedback counts with their dates and population, so readers can tell what the figures cover. There have been no reported cases in this sample of the preference merging profiles, restoring private windows, or copying itself through Finch Tabs sync; phrase that only as an observation about this sample, not as proof that such a case could never occur. Don’t add technical causes for the questions or claim that the interface has been changed. No fix, approval, or decision to expand the beta is in these notes.

I’d like one connected, ordinary internal update with a short title and a clear final section. A numbered section would be useful if it makes the explanation easier to follow, perhaps with a section on the setting and another on what the early feedback does and doesn’t show. Keep the voice measured and practical rather than promotional. Avoid a table because the information is short enough to read in prose. The final section should retain the complete assessment and its limits: the 12-day period ending May 18, 214 opted-in desktop profiles, 17 support messages and the breakdown, the limited audience, and what cannot be inferred from those figures. It should also say that the next evidence review is scheduled for May 21 and will check whether the same kinds of questions continue as the beta proceeds. That review is scheduled, not completed, and the notes do not say what it will find. End on that next check and its scope, rather than adding a recommendation or an overall verdict. Please organize all of this into the prompt, including the requested deliverable and constraints, without filling in anything beyond these notes.", "output": "Write a self-contained internal product update for the product, support, and documentation teams about the restore preference in Finch Tabs, a fictional browser extension. Give the update a short title, use connected prose, and finish with a clear final section. Numbered sections may be used if helpful. Do not use a table.

Explain the preference before discussing feedback. The setting is called “Restore the last tab group when the browser starts” and appears under Settings > Startup in Finch Tabs version 2.8.1. It is off by default. Users must turn it on and save it; installing version 2.8.1 does not change existing users’ settings. The checkbox can be changed without restarting the browser, but the saved choice takes effect only at the next full browser launch. Make clear that changing the checkbox does not cause an immediate restoration.

Describe the setting’s scope precisely. It restores only the last non-private tab group in the same browser profile. It does not restore private windows or combine tab groups from different profiles. The preference is available when the Startup choice is “New tab.” If another Startup choice is selected, the checkbox is unavailable. If a user enables the preference and later selects a different Startup choice, the saved preference remains on, but it is not used while that other choice is active. Selecting “New tab” again makes the saved preference applicable at the next full launch. The setting is local to each browser profile and is not copied to other profiles or devices through Finch Tabs sync. Do not portray different values on two devices as evidence that the setting is broken.

Report the current beta status without suggesting a broader release. The desktop beta for version 2.8.1 is available to 15 percent of eligible profiles, and its staged rollout began on May 6. It is limited to desktop installations that are not managed by an organization. The mobile companion does not have this preference, and there is no confirmed expansion date in the notes. Product has requested an update about the preference and initial feedback, not an announcement of a rollout decision.

Include the early assessment with its dates, population, and limitations. It covers the first 12 days after the beta began, through May 18, and includes 214 opted-in desktop profiles. During that period, support logged 17 messages mentioning the preference: 9 asked where to find the checkbox, 5 described expecting restoration before the next full launch, and 3 asked why the preference was unavailable on a managed installation. Present these as message counts, not counts of people or confirmed defects. Do not infer how common these expectations are among all Finch Tabs users.

Include the support note, “I want my work tabs back, but not the window I closed on purpose.” Identify it as a comment about the preference’s intended scope, not as evidence that private windows were restored or as a general conclusion from customers. The sample contains no reported cases of the preference merging profiles, restoring private windows, or copying itself through Finch Tabs sync. State this only as an observation about this sample, not proof that such a case could never happen. Do not invent technical causes for the questions or claim that the interface has changed. The notes contain no fix, approval, or decision to expand the beta.

In the final section, retain the full assessment and its limits: the 12-day period ending May 18, the 214 opted-in desktop profiles, all 17 support messages and their breakdown, the beta’s limited audience, and what cannot be inferred from the figures. State that the next evidence review is scheduled for May 21 to check whether the same kinds of questions continue as the beta proceeds. Make clear that the review is scheduled, not completed, and that the notes do not say what it will find. End with that next check and its scope, without adding a recommendation or overall verdict."}]
